core.title: Use the shared meaning of WMBT (advisory semantic anchor)
core.given: The term WMBT (What Must Be True) is used, asked about, or authored, in any context
core.then: Use this one meaning: a falsifiable statement of a single outcome that must hold for an artifact — scoped to one object of control along one dimension, direction, and lens — declared with an id and a statement, and paired with the acceptances that prove it, including at least one smoke acceptance.
prefer: For the enforceable parts, follow the referenced rules that decompose this meaning: planner.wmbt.shape (id, statement, proving artifacts), planner.wmbt.object-of-control, planner.wmbt.dimension-/direction-/lens-selection and planner.wmbt.splitting-rules (single axis), planner.wmbt.statement-template, planner.wmbt.must-have-smoke-acceptance.
avoid: Using WMBT for an unfalsifiable or multi-outcome statement.
Treating this anchor as a validator; compliance is checked through the enforceable nodes that require this anchor.
core.why: A WMBT needs one stable meaning so every WMBT rule checks the same concept. This anchor is advisory: it enforces nothing directly and is transitively protected by the rule nodes that require it.
evidence: No direct check on this node; compliance is established by the enforceable nodes that require this anchor: planner.wmbt.shape, planner.wmbt.object-of-control, planner.wmbt.dimension-selection, planner.wmbt.direction-selection, planner.wmbt.lens-selection, planner.wmbt.splitting-rules, planner.wmbt.statement-template, planner.wmbt.must-have-smoke-acceptance.
Reviewer may confirm that uses of the term WMBT match the definition in then.
verification: Advisory semantic anchor: this node is a definitional anchor with a stable meaning, not a check — no detector or validator of this rule reports findings directly against it; it is transitively protected by the enforceable rules that require it, so no detector should report findings on this node directly.

The meaning is verified only through the referenced rules that decompose the term: well-shaped (declares its id, its statement, and the artifacts that prove the statement), single-object-of-control, single-axis (one dimension, one direction, one lens), statement-formed (follows the statement template), and smoke-covered (at least one smoke acceptance); a realization binds validators to those rules, never to this node.

fires: Someone asks what a WMBT is or how one is shaped (no diff involved).
A planner writes or revises a WMBT, in any artifact.
A doc, review or acceptance discussion uses the term WMBT and needs its meaning.
doesNotFire: Work that neither uses nor touches the WMBT concept (e.g. implementing code against acceptances with no reference to WMBTs).
Verifier runs looking for findings: this anchor emits no findings itself; the referenced rules do.

Term decomposition mapping each part of the meaning (well-shaped, single-object-of-control, single-axis, statement-formed, smoke-covered) to the sibling rules that enforce it; its generic form is core verification entry 2. The referenced ids are convention pointers, not stack specifics.

Task-term trigger, observable now. The Bun note (any task text using or asking about the term; independent of phase, operation or artifact location) is carried by the neutral fact shape only as fact/values/observability, so its content is preserved here and in fires; it names nothing stack-specific.

Optional, non-exclusive diff-level trigger (a WMBT entry added or changed in any artifact), needs a new observer. The Bun note that it is optional and not required for activation cannot be carried in the neutral fact shape and is preserved in this note and in neutralityNotes; recognizing 'a WMBT entry' in a diff is left to the realization's plan-artifact profile data.

neutralityNotes: The Bun rewrite is already stack-neutral: it is a definitional anchor over artifact-level concepts (WMBT, acceptances, smoke acceptance) and names no stack, runtime, framework, language, path or file kind, so the core keeps its agent-facing text essentially verbatim and needs no profile values (profileRequirements empty). Two caveats. (1) The references to sibling conventions (planner.wmbt.shape, -object-of-control, -dimension/-direction/-lens-selection, -splitting-rules, -statement-template, -must-have-smoke-acceptance) are convention ids, not stack specifics; the core assumes the same convention family exists in any realization, and a realization re-points the references if its family uses different ids without changing the obligation. (2) activation.facts[1]'s note field (optional, non-exclusive diff trigger, not required for activation) has no slot in the neutral fact shape; its meaning is preserved in the classification note, in the fire 'Someone asks what a WMBT is ... (no diff involved)', and here. The optional diff observer's recognition of a WMBT entry would use the realization's plan-artifact profile data, which the core itself does not reference.
